model_plain: Every registered DC voter is mailed a ballot automatically. Mail it back (postage is prepaid), put it in a drop box, or skip it and vote in person at any Vote Center in the District. Most contests are ranked-choice this year: you rank candidates instead of picking one.

deadlines.rule: The regular deadline was Tuesday, October 13, 2026 (21 days before the election) for online and DMV registrations and updates. That date has passed. Applications received after it are held until after the election. You can still register in person and vote the same day (see below).
Paper applications had to be received by DCBOE by Tuesday, October 13, 2026 (not postmarked). That date has passed.

Same-day registration. You can register and vote at any Early Vote Center from Monday, October 26 through Sunday, November 1 (8:30 AM to 7:00 PM), or at any Vote Center on Election Day, November 3, from 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Bring proof that you live in DC.

registration.same_day_notes: Go to any Early Vote Center (Oct 26 to Nov 1) or any Vote Center on November 3. Bring ONE proof of residence showing your name and current DC address. DCBOE accepts: a current government-issued photo ID; a utility bill (water, gas, electric, cable, internet, phone or cell) issued within 90 days; a bank or credit union statement within 90 days; a paycheck or pay stub within 90 days that includes the employer's name, address and phone; a government document or check from a federal or DC agency (other than DCBOE) within 90 days; a current lease or rental agreement; an occupancy statement from a DC homeless shelter within 90 days; or a tuition or housing bill from a DC college for the current term. You must have lived in DC at least 30 days before the election (since October 4, 2026). Source: https://dcboe.org/Voters/Register-To-Vote/Register-to-Vote
registration.still_possible_now: Yes. The October 13 regular deadline has passed, but DC lets you register in person and vote right then at any Early Vote Center from October 26 to November 1, or at any Vote Center on November 3 until 8:00 PM. Bring proof of your DC address. If you think you're already registered, check at apps.dcboe.org/VRS first.

mail_ballot.who_gets_one: Automatic. DC mails a ballot to every registered voter; no request or excuse is needed. DCBOE began mailing ballots on Monday, September 28, 2026. If yours hasn't arrived, call 1-866-DCVOTES (1-866-328-6837) or 202-727-2525, track it at votedc.ballottrax.net, or just vote in person at any Vote Center. If you got the wrong ward's ballot, DCBOE says to call immediately.

request_deadline.rule: You don't have to request a ballot; everyone gets one. The DCBOE calendar lists Monday, October 19, 2026 as the deadline for receipt of ballot requests from non-military voters (for example, to have one sent to a different address). After that, get a replacement in person or vote in person. For a lost or spoiled ballot, DCBOE says to call 1-866-DCVOTES immediately.

return_deadline.time: 8:00 PM ET for drop boxes, Vote Centers and the DCBOE office; mailed ballots must be postmarked by November 3 and received by Friday, November 13

return_options: Any of 55 mail ballot drop boxes across all eight wards (open since Friday, October 9 at 11:00 AM; they lock at 8:00 PM on November 3)
Mail (USPS), postage prepaid, postmarked by November 3; must arrive by November 13
Any of the 25 Early Vote Centers, October 26 to November 1, 8:30 AM to 7:00 PM
Any Vote Center on Election Day, November 3, 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM
DCBOE headquarters, 1015 Half Street SE (also has a drop box)
mail_ballot.signature_witness_rules: Sign and date the Voter's Oath on the back of the return envelope. No witness or notary. DCBOE: 'You must sign the Voter's Oath in order for your vote to count!' Put only your own ballot in your envelope; if it contains anyone else's ballot, none of them count. Don't tape the envelope shut. First-time voters who registered by mail or online without a DC DMV or Social Security match must include a photocopy of ID (photo ID, or a utility bill, bank statement, government check or paycheck dated within 90 days) or the ballot is treated as a special (provisional) ballot. Source: https://www.dcboe.org/voters/casting-your-vote/mail-ballot-instructions
mail_ballot.cure_process: If DCBOE sends you a notice, return the signed certificate and any requested proof promptly, following the deadline in your letter. You may email, mail or deliver the response to DCBOE. Its FAQ says seven days after Election Day (November 10), but its 2026 calendar lists November 19 for mail-ballot cures. These official dates still conflict as of October 19. Aim to fix a mail ballot by November 10 and call 202-727-2525 if your notice is unclear. Sign up for BallotTrax alerts so you hear about problems. For a special (provisional) ballot, provide requested proof promptly: the special-ballot FAQ says 5 PM on the Thursday after Election Day (November 5), while the 2026 calendar says November 10. Call DCBOE to confirm your deadline; do not wait for the later date.
mail_ballot.mail_cutoff_advice: Postmarks count in DC, but a missing or late postmark is a real risk (DCBOE had to clarify USPS postmark rules during the June primary). Mail by about Tuesday, October 27 at the latest. From then on, use a drop box: 55 of them, open around the clock until 8:00 PM on November 3. A mailed ballot postmarked by November 3 still has to arrive at DCBOE by Friday, November 13. If you mail it, ask a post office counter clerk for a free manual postmark when you hand it over. This does not extend the receipt deadline.

early_in_person.hours_note: Monday, October 26 through Sunday, November 1, 2026, every day including the weekend, 8:30 AM to 7:00 PM. 25 Early Vote Centers, two to four per ward (for example Columbia Heights Community Center, MLK Library, Cleveland Park Library, Turkey Thicket, Sherwood Rec, Deanwood Rec; note THEARC is an Election Day-only Vote Center, not an early site). Any DC voter can use any center. All 25 also operate on Election Day. You can register on the spot with proof of residence. Full list at the DCBOE PDF below or earlyvoting.dcboe.org.

election_day.in_line_rule: DCBOE: 'All voters who are in line at 8:00 p.m. may cast a ballot.' Drop boxes also lock at 8:00 PM, and mailed ballots must be postmarked that day.

accepted: Most registered voters: no ID. You state your name and address. (ACLU of DC: 'No specific ID is required to vote in person.')

First-time voters who registered by mail or online and couldn't be matched to a DC DMV or Social Security record: a current government-issued photo ID, or a utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck or other government document with your name and current DC address, dated within 90 days

Same-day registrants: one proof of DC residence from the list in same_day_notes (photo ID, utility bill, bank statement, pay stub, government document, lease, shelter letter, or college housing or tuition bill)
id_rules.no_id_option: If you're flagged as a first-time voter needing ID and don't have it, you vote a special (provisional) ballot and must bring the document to DCBOE so it counts. Go by 5:00 PM on Thursday, November 5: DCBOE's special ballot FAQ says you have 'two days following the election to show your ID,' while the 2026 calendar lists Tuesday, November 10. Most DC voters are never asked for ID. Sources: https://dcboe.org/Voters/Register-To-Vote/Register-to-Vote and https://www.acludc.org/how-to-vote-in-the-november-3-2026-d-c-general-election/

in_the_booth.phones_detail: DC has no law against phones in a Vote Center, and DCBOE does not ban them. Using your phone to read your own notes or sample ballot is fine. A DCBOE spokeswoman has said officials 'discourage people from taking pictures but won't do anything to stop them' (FOX 5, 2016). Don't photograph other voters or poll workers. No 2026 DCBOE statement was found; confidence is 'sourced' for this field. Source: https://www.fox5dc.com/news/ballot-selfies-in-dc-md-va-are-they-legal
in_the_booth.notes_detail: Nothing in DC law or DCBOE rules bars a printed or handwritten list or a marked-up sample ballot in the booth. With ranked-choice ballots this year, a written list of your rankings is a good idea. The limit is electioneering: you can't display or hand out campaign material inside the Vote Center or within the no-campaigning zone around it. Sample ballots for every ward are on DCBOE's 2026 Elections page. Source: https://dcboe.org/elections/2026-elections
in_the_booth.apparel_rule: DC bars campaigning near Vote Centers, which in practice means poll workers will ask you to cover or remove candidate shirts, hats or buttons before you go in. The exact distance and the 2026 DCBOE notice were not located this run; treat as 'sourced.' Easiest rule: leave campaign gear at home.

gotchas.text: Ranked-choice voting is on most of your ballot. In each RCV contest you'll see columns labeled 1st, 2nd, 3rd and so on. Fill in ONE oval per column: your favorite under 1st, your backup under 2nd. Don't put two candidates in the same column, don't mark the same candidate twice, and don't skip a column (skipping more than one can make your vote inactive in that contest). You can rank just one if you want. If nobody has a majority of first choices, the last-place candidate is dropped and those ballots move to their next choice, round by round. Ranking a backup never hurts your first choice. Contests with only two candidates (Council Chair, Attorney General, Shadow Senator, Shadow Rep) are normal pick-one votes.
gotchas.short: Fill one oval per column: your favorite under 1st, your backup under 2nd.

gotchas.text: The at-large Council race fills TWO seats, but your ballot can only help elect ONE of them. DCBOE counts each ballot once, for your highest-ranked candidate still in the race, and keeps eliminating last place until two are left. Once your top pick is one of the final two, your lower rankings never transfer. By DC's charter only one of the two winners can be a Democrat. So if you want to influence which non-Democrat wins the second seat, rank that candidate FIRST. (Hill Rag, Oct 12; GGWash, Oct 1; DCBOE RCV page.)
gotchas.short: At-large Council: your ballot can help elect only one of the two seats.

gotchas.text: The regular registration deadline (October 13) has passed, but you can still register and vote in person at any Early Vote Center (Oct 26 to Nov 1) or any Vote Center on November 3. Bring proof of your DC address.
gotchas.short: Register and vote at any Vote Center; bring proof of your DC address.

gotchas.text: Postmarks count, but don't lean on them. Mail by about October 27 or use one of 55 drop boxes (open 24 hours until 8:00 PM on November 3). No stamp needed. Sign and date the oath on the envelope or your ballot won't count. A mailed ballot must also arrive by November 13.
gotchas.short: Sign and date the envelope oath; after about Oct 27, use a drop box.

gotchas.text: There IS one ballot measure this year: Initiative 86, the foie gras ban. It's at the very end of the ballot, after the ANC race. And you can vote at ANY Vote Center in the District, not just the one near you; early voting uses 25 sites and Election Day uses 75. Polls are open 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM. DC law also gives employees and students up to 2 hours of paid leave to vote.
gotchas.short: Initiative 86, the foie gras ban, is the last item, after the ANC race.

situations.question: I moved to a new address in DC.
situations.short: Update your address at any Vote Center with proof of your new address, and vote a regular ballot.
situations.answer: Update your address at any Vote Center during early voting (October 26 to November 1) or on Election Day. Show proof of your new address, fill out a Registration Update Form, and you'll vote a regular ballot.
steps: Bring one proof: DC DMV ID, lease, utility bill, bank statement, paycheck or government document (bills and statements dated within 90 days).
The address on your proof has to match the new address on the form.
No proof with you? You'll vote a special ballot and have to bring proof to DCBOE afterward.

situations.question: I moved out of DC.
situations.short: Register in your new state instead, and don't return the DC ballot mailed to your old address.
situations.answer: You vote where you live now, so register in your new state instead, and don't return the DC ballot mailed to your old address. Some states still take registrations or offer same-day registration, so check today.
steps: Look up your new state's rules and deadline at vote.gov.
When you register, list your old DC address so your DC registration can be canceled.

situations.question: I'm not registered yet.
situations.short: Register and vote the same day at any Vote Center; bring proof of your DC address.
situations.answer: The October 13 deadline has passed, but DC has same-day registration. Go to any Vote Center during early voting (October 26 to November 1, 8:30 AM to 7 PM) or on Election Day (7 AM to 8 PM), bring proof of your DC address, and you'll register and vote a regular ballot.
steps: Proof: DC DMV ID, lease, utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, government document, student housing or tuition bill, or shelter letter.
You need to have lived in DC since at least October 4.
Check first at apps.dcboe.org/VRS in case you're already registered.

situations.question: The lookup can’t find me.
situations.short: The lookup needs your name exactly as registered: try your last name with the hyphen, a space, and joined.
situations.answer: DC’s lookup asks for your name, birth date, and the last four digits of your Social Security number, DMV ID or voter ID. If none of those fit, the Board of Elections says to call 202-727-2525.
steps: Try your last name with the hyphen, with a space instead, and run together, and leave out any middle name or suffix.
Still nothing? Call your county election office. A failed search doesn’t mean you’re not registered; records can lag.

situations.question: I went to the wrong polling place.
situations.short: There's no wrong Vote Center: you can vote at any one in DC, early or on Election Day.
situations.answer: There's no wrong Vote Center in DC. You can vote at any Vote Center in the District, early or on Election Day, no matter which ward you live in.
steps: Early voting: 25 centers, October 26 to November 1, 8:30 AM to 7 PM.
Election Day: 75 Vote Centers, 7 AM to 8 PM.
Find one near you at earlyvoting.dcboe.org or on dcboe.org.

situations.question: My mail ballot never came, or I lost it.
situations.short: Vote in person at any Vote Center instead, or call (202) 727-2525 if you're away.
situations.answer: Vote in person at any Vote Center instead; DCBOE says if your mail ballot hasn't come 7 days before Election Day, plan to vote in person. If you asked for an absentee ballot because you're away and lost it, call (202) 727-2525 and they'll mail a new one.
steps: Check its status at votedc.ballottrax.net.
Early voting runs October 26 to November 1, 8:30 AM to 7 PM; Election Day is 7 AM to 8 PM.
Questions: 1-866-DCVOTES (1-866-328-6837).

situations.question: I made a mistake on my ballot.
situations.short: Ask a worker for a new ballot; on a mail ballot, call (202) 727-2525 or vote in person instead.
situations.answer: At a Vote Center, tell an election worker right away; they'll cancel it and give you a new one, up to three ballots in all. On a mail ballot, call DCBOE at (202) 727-2525 and they'll mail you a new one, or just vote in person instead.

situations.question: I got a mail ballot, but I want to vote in person.
situations.short: Write "Voting in Person" on the unopened ballot, hand it in at any Vote Center, and get a new one.
situations.answer: Write "Voting in Person" on the unopened mail ballot, then hand it to an election worker at any Vote Center or drop it in a DCBOE drop box, and you'll get a new ballot to vote. If you already returned a voted mail ballot, you've voted; trying again means a special ballot.
steps: Or fill out the mail ballot at home and drop it off at any Vote Center without waiting in line.
Track it at votedc.ballottrax.net.

situations.question: I don't have an ID.
situations.short: Most DC voters are never asked for ID; if you're flagged, vote a special ballot and bring ID afterward.
situations.answer: Most DC voters are never asked for ID. If you're a first-time voter flagged for ID and don't have it, you'll vote a special ballot and need to bring ID to DCBOE afterward so it counts.
steps: Accepted: a government photo ID, or a utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, government check or government document with your name and address, dated within 90 days.
Bring it to DCBOE at 1015 Half Street SE by 5 PM on Thursday, November 5 to be safe. The 2026 calendar allows until Tuesday, November 10.

situations.question: My name changed since I registered.
situations.short: Update it at any Vote Center with a Registration Update Form; no proof of address needed.
situations.answer: Update it at any Vote Center during early voting or on Election Day by filling out a Registration Update Form. You don't need proof of address for a name change, and you'll vote a regular ballot.

situations.question: I'm a college student.
situations.short: If you study in DC, register and vote the same day at any Vote Center with your tuition bill.
situations.answer: If you go to school in DC, you can register and vote the same day at any Vote Center, using a student housing statement or tuition bill as proof. If you're registered in DC but at school somewhere else, ask for your ballot to be mailed to your school by Monday, October 19.
steps: Use the Mail Ballot Request form on dcboe.org.
Mail your ballot so it's postmarked by November 3; it must arrive within 10 days.
Track it at votedc.ballottrax.net.

situations.question: I'll be away on Election Day.
situations.short: Fill out your mail ballot and return it before you leave; drop boxes take ballots through 8 PM Nov 3.
situations.answer: If you have your mail ballot, fill it out and return it before leaving. Drop boxes accept ballots through 8 PM on November 3. If you need an absentee ballot sent away from your DC residence, request it by October 19. After that deadline, call DCBOE at 202-727-2525 about your options, or vote in person during October 26 to November 1 or on November 3 if you are in DC.
steps: Or vote early in person any day October 26 to November 1, 8:30 AM to 7 PM.
Mail by about October 27; postage is prepaid.
The request form is on dcboe.org's Mail Ballot Request page.

situations.question: I'm in line when the polls close.
situations.short: Stay in line: everyone in line at 8 PM on Election Day gets to vote.
situations.answer: Stay in line. Everyone in line at 8 PM on Election Day gets to vote. Drop boxes lock at 8 PM, though.

situations.question: There's a problem with the signature on my mail ballot.
situations.short: Sign the certificate in the Board of Elections' letter and send it back right away.
situations.answer: DCBOE will send you a letter, and BallotTrax alerts too, explaining the problem and your deadline. Sign the certificate in the letter and send it back right away; DCBOE's FAQ says cures are accepted up to seven days after the election (November 10), though the 2026 calendar lists November 19.
steps: Email the signed certificate to dcabsentee@dcboe.org, or mail or deliver it to 1015 Half Street SE, #750.
If the letter asks for proof of residence, send that with the certificate.
Sign up for alerts at votedc.ballottrax.net.

situations.question: They told me to vote a provisional ballot.
situations.short: DC calls it a special ballot, and it counts if you're eligible; bring any missing proof or ID afterward.
situations.answer: DC calls it a special ballot. It's counted if DCBOE decides you're eligible, even if it won't change the outcome; if you were missing proof of address or ID, bring it to DCBOE afterward.
steps: Bring proof to DCBOE, 1015 Half Street SE, by 5 PM on Thursday, November 5 to be safe. The 2026 calendar allows until November 10.
Check the result on dcboe.org's Special Ballot Status page or at 1-866-DCVOTES.

situations.question: How do I check that my ballot was counted?
situations.short: Track your mail ballot with BallotTrax; for a special ballot, check the Special Ballot Status page on dcboe.org.
situations.answer: Track your mail ballot at votedc.ballottrax.net and opt in to text, email or voice alerts; it also flags problems you need to fix. For a special ballot, use the Special Ballot Status page on dcboe.org or call 1-866-DCVOTES.

heads_up.text: Rank up to five candidates in ranked-choice races. Use one candidate per column and rank each candidate only once.
Two at-large council members win, but your ballot counts for one candidate at a time. Rank candidates rather than choosing two equal first choices.
